theory.intro: A **progressive** income tax table splits taxable income into brackets. Each rate applies only to the income above that bracket's lower boundary. Find the bracket, then the excess, then the tax. Use the table supplied in each question: the Australian table here is the historical $2022$–$23$ table, and other questions use fictional countries.
facts: $\text{Excess}=\text{Taxable income}-\text{Upper limit of the previous bracket}$
A rate written as '$19$ cents for each $\$1$' is $0.19$ as a decimal, and '$32.5$ cents for each $\$1$' is $0.325$.
In the supplied historical Australian table, the first bracket is taxed at nil, so a taxable income of $\$18\,200$ or less has $\$0$ income tax payable.
A bracket's **base tax** is the total tax payable on all the income in the brackets below it.

With these supplied tables, considering income tax only, moving into a higher bracket still leaves some of the extra income after tax. The higher rate applies only to the extra dollars above that boundary.

workedExamples.question_text:
Use these supplied historical $2022$–$23$ tax rules: income up to $\$18\,200$ is taxed at nil; $\$18\,201$ to $\$45\,000$ is taxed at $19$ cents for each dollar over $\$18\,200$; $\$45\,001$ to $\$120\,000$ has base tax $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents for each dollar over $\$45\,000$.
Find the bracket and tax payable for (a) $\$17\,400$, (b) $\$35\,600$ and (c) $\$72\,000$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) First bracket: tax $=\$0$.
(b) Second bracket. Excess $=35\,600-18\,200=17\,400$.
Tax $=0.19\times17\,400=\$3306$.
(c) Third bracket. Excess $=72\,000-45\,000=27\,000$.
Tax $=5092+0.325\times27\,000=\$13\,867$. The base tax already includes the tax on earlier brackets.

workedExamples.question_text: Use these supplied historical tax rows: $\$120\,001$–$\$180\,000$: base tax $\$29\,467$ plus $37$ cents per dollar over $\$120\,000$; above $\$180\,000$: base tax $\$51\,667$ plus $45$ cents per dollar over $\$180\,000$. Find tax payable on (a) exactly $\$180\,000$ and (b) $\$204\,000$.

Use these supplied historical $2022$–$23$ tax rules: income up to $\$18\,200$ is taxed at nil; $\$18\,201$ to $\$45\,000$ is taxed at $19$ cents for each dollar over $\$18\,200$; $\$45\,001$ to $\$120\,000$ has base tax $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents for each dollar over $\$45\,000$.
(a) Compare taxable incomes of $\$60\,000$ and $\$66\,000$. How much extra tax is paid on the higher income?
(b) A pay rise increases taxable income from $\$43\,000$ to $\$49\,000$. Find the extra tax and how much of the rise remains after income tax.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Both are in the third bracket. Extra tax $=0.325\times(66\,000-60\,000)=\$1950$.
(b) Tax before $=0.19\times(43\,000-18\,200)=\$4712$.
Tax after $=5092+0.325\times(49\,000-45\,000)=\$6392$.
Extra tax $=6392-4712=\$1680$.
Rise after income tax $=6000-1680=\$4320$. The higher rate applies only to income above $\$45\,000$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Use these supplied historical $2022$–$23$ tax rules: income up to $\$18\,200$ is taxed at nil; $\$18\,201$ to $\$45\,000$ is taxed at $19$ cents for each dollar over $\$18\,200$; $\$45\,001$ to $\$120\,000$ has base tax $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents for each dollar over $\$45\,000$.
(a) A person pays $\$11\,917$ income tax. Find the taxable income.
(b) Another person has taxable income $\$80\,000$. Find the tax as a percentage of that income, to one decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $11\,917$ is between the base taxes $5092$ and $29\,467$, so use the third bracket.
Tax on excess $=11\,917-5092=6825$.
Excess $=6825\div0.325=21\,000$.
Taxable income $=45\,000+21\,000=\$66\,000$.
(b) Tax $=5092+0.325\times(80\,000-45\,000)=\$16\,467$.
Percentage $=\frac{16\,467}{80\,000}\times100\%\approx20.6\%$. This percentage uses the total tax and whole income, rather than the bracket rate.

workedExamples.question_text:
A fictional country has these supplied tax rules: income up to $\$18\,000$: nil; $\$18\,001$–$\$48\,000$: $20$ cents per dollar over $\$18\,000$; above $\$48\,000$: base tax $\$a$ plus $y$ cents per dollar over $\$48\,000$.
(a) Find $a$, the total tax at the previous bracket's upper boundary.
(b) A taxable income of $\$62\,000$ has tax $\$10\,900$. Find $y$.

In a fictional tax table, income up to $\$20\,000$ is taxed at nil; the next $\$10\,000$ at $20$ cents per dollar; and income from $\$30\,001$ to $\$80\,000$ has base tax $\$2000$ plus $20$ cents per dollar over $\$30\,000$. A person in this last bracket pays exactly $12\%$ of taxable income in tax. Find the taxable income.

foundation.question_text:
A high-school teacher has a taxable income of $\$79\,400$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to state which tax bracket her taxable income falls into (first, second, third, fourth or fifth).
foundation.solution_text:
$\$79\,400$ is more than $\$45\,000$ and not more than $\$120\,000$.
It lies in the third bracket.

foundation.solution_text:
1. **Determine the tax bracket**
$\$31\,000$ lies in the second bracket ($\$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000$).
2. **Calculate the excess**

development.question_text:
An engineer with a taxable income of $\$117\,000$ is given a pay rise that takes her taxable income to $\$126\,000$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to find how much extra income tax she pays as a result of the rise, to the nearest cent.

mastery.question_text:
The table shows the personal income tax rates for a different country.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$22\,000 & \text{Nil} \\ \$22\,001\text{ to }\$58\,000 & 20\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$22\,000 \\ \$58\,001\text{ to }\$140\,000 & \$7200\text{ plus }33\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$58\,000 \\ \$140\,001\text{ and over} & \$34\,260\text{ plus }y\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$140\,000 \end{array}$
A resident with a taxable income of $\$180\,000$ pays $\$50\,660$ in income tax.
Find the value of $y$.

The table shows the personal income tax rates for a different country.
The base tax of a bracket is the total tax payable on all the income in the brackets below it.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$25\,000 & \text{Nil} \\ \$25\,001\text{ to }\$70\,000 & 30\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$25\,000 \\ \$70\,001\text{ to }\$150\,000 & \$a\text{ plus }38\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$70\,000 \\ \$150\,001\text{ and over} & \$b\text{ plus }47\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$150\,000 \end{array}$
Find the values of $a$ and $b$, each to the nearest dollar.
mastery.solution_text:
$a$ is the total tax payable on a taxable income of $\$70\,000$.
$a=0.30\times(70\,000-25\,000)$
$=0.30\times45\,000$
$=\$13\,500$
$b$ is the total tax payable on a taxable income of $\$150\,000$.
$b=13\,500+0.38\times(150\,000-70\,000)$
$=13\,500+0.38\times80\,000$
$=\$43\,900$

mastery.question_text:
A nurse manager's income tax payable is exactly $20\%$ of her taxable income, and her taxable income lies in the third bracket.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to find her taxable income, to the nearest dollar.

A teacher says: "If my taxable income goes from $\$119\,000$ to $\$121\,000$ I move into the $37$c bracket, so all of my income is taxed at $37$c and I end up worse off."
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to find the income tax payable at each taxable income, and explain her error.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Tax on }\$119\,000=5092+0.325\times74\,000$
$=\$29\,142.00$
$\text{Tax on }\$121\,000=29\,467+0.37\times1000$
$=\$29\,837.00$
$\text{Extra tax}=29\,837-29\,142$
$=\$695.00$
The $37$c rate applies only to the $\$1000$ above $\$120\,000$, not to the whole income, so the extra $\$2000$ of income costs only $\$695$ in tax and she keeps $\$1305$ of it.
